findings.evidence: `rg -n "@\[expose\].*coinvariantsEquivHom|coinvariantsEquivHom_apply|coinvariantsEquivHom_symm_apply_coe"` shows `@[expose] noncomputable def coinvariantsEquivHom` at line 199 and the public characterization lemmas at lines 226 and 234.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]`; keep the body hidden and prove the needed computation lemmas (`coinvariantsEquivHom_apply`, `coinvariantsEquivHom_symm_apply_coe`, and invariant specializations) without requiring downstream unfolding.
findings.issue: `coinvariantsEquivHom` is marked `@[expose]`, exposing the implementation of the universal-property equivalence even though the file already provides public apply/inverse characterizations.

findings.evidence: `mem_coinvariants`, `mapCoinvariants_coe_apply`, and `mapCoinvariants_comp` are `@[simp]` at lines 82, 132, and 146, while the invariant parallels at lines 264, 289, and 304 lack the annotation.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp]` to `mem_invariants`, `mapInvariants_coe_apply`, and `mapInvariants_comp` unless one of them causes a demonstrated loop.
findings.issue: Invariant-specific normal-form lemmas are not tagged for automation: `mem_invariants`, `mapInvariants_coe_apply`, and `mapInvariants_comp` are the characteristic restatements users will expect `simp` to use, parallel to the coinvariant lemmas.

summary: The new surface is mostly characterized, but it exposes an equivalence body unnecessarily and leaves invariant-specific normal-form lemmas out of simp automation.
